capex_override.reason: DATA_GAP:capex — capex missing for FY2023, FY2024, FY2025 of the last 3 in EDGAR companyfacts under every candidate tag the engine reads (the filed values through FY2022 came via PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment, $18.967M in FY2022); the filer's own cash-flow statement reports this capex line for all three missing years. The engine applies this single FY2025 filing value to every missing period; against the same statement's true per-year values it overstates FY2023 capex by $44.503M (true $15.028M) and FY2024 capex by $29.835M (true $29.696M) — both in the conservative direction of lowering owner's earnings. The value is 3.14x the last filed capex value ($18.967M, FY2022), inside the engine's 0.1x-10x band.

moat_against: No pricing power: royalties are a price-taker claim on oil and gas prices
Volumes depend on third-party operators' drilling pace and on Permian depletion
Single-basin concentration: essentially all value sits in West Texas
Long-run hydrocarbon demand decline caps the terminal story
Water segment is capital-intensive and competitive, unlike the royalty segment; growth acreage is now bought at market prices ($454.244M of royalty-interest acquisitions in FY2025)
moat_for: Irreplaceable Permian acreage: ~882,000 surface acres plus perpetual nonparticipating royalty interests (~224,000 net royalty acres) that cannot be replicated
Royalties bear no well capex or operating-expense burden — a structural cost advantage no producer can match
Same acreage monetized repeatedly across the well lifecycle: easements, leases, caliche/sand, sourced water and produced-water royalties
Scale water network in the Permian (produced-water royalty volumes of 4.9 million bbl/d in Q2 2026)
Debt-free balance sheet with cash on hand — survives commodity troughs without dilution or distress
moat_justification: Irreplaceable Permian land and perpetual royalty acreage with a zero-cost royalty structure and a debt-free balance sheet — a strong asset moat — but the company is a price-taker on oil and gas, volumes depend on third-party operators and Permian depletion, and essentially all value is concentrated in one basin facing long-run hydrocarbon decline, so it is strong (7), not wide (9-10).
name: Texas Pacific Land Corporation
one_liner: Superb royalty asset, moat 7/10, but the price pays for land scarcity, not owner's earnings — weighted IRR 7.24% (Tier D), weighted IV@15% $116.50 vs the $354.50 price; it clears 15% only at or below $116.50.
sector: Energy / Oil & gas royalties, land and water
